pages.lesson:
LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.5: Interactive Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Interactive Speaking. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How else do you communicate without use of speech?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
2. use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
3. use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication
4. use specific vocabulary and expressions to engage in simple conversations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Interactive Speaking helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to and sing songs with vocabulary on formal greetings and introductions,
2. Play mimicry games to acquire non-verbal communication skills,
3. Communication and Collaboration: These are developed as the learner listens keenly and actively engages in the conversation.
4. Listen to audiovisual materials to identify members of the extended family by relation, (grand parent,oncle, tante, neveu, beaux parents...)
5. Listen to audio documents as they complete information on a set of family trees,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How else do you communicate without use of speech?
2. Why is attention important when listening?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
